Hi Sean —

We observed elevated 5xx rates and sustained latency spikes against Redwood's transaction generation endpoint between ~01:12–01:57 UTC on 2026-10-28. Our monitoring shows ~45 minutes of partial failures (payment-authorize calls returning 503) and request latencies spiking to 4–6s (baseline ~120ms). This caused payment retries and an estimated 0.8% revenue impact during that window.

Attached: mp_errors_oct28.log (sampled error traces and timestamps).

Can you confirm the root cause and whether this qualifies for an SLA credit? Per our contract, we expect 99.95% availability and would like an explicit credit calculation and timeline for remediation.

Subject: Re: Transaction API errors + high latency 2026-10-28 (requesting SLA credit)

Hi Alex —

Really sorry about the disruption. We saw elevated error rates in our telemetry as well and have started an investigation. Initial observations:
- A routing maintenance activity for our regional traffic tier was scheduled 2026-10-28 01:00–01:45 UTC (internal routing resync).
- We also observed a small burst of external BGP instability in one upstream provider at ~01:15–01:35 UTC in our telemetry.

To proceed we need:
1) Exact list of affected transaction IDs/timestamps (a sample is fine) — helps correlate to our traces.
2) Any client-side retry timestamps (if available).

We're opening an incident page with the current timeline and will add logs. Public incident: https://status.redwood.ai/incident/1267

I've attached a snapshot of our preliminary SLA calc (slo_routing_maintenance_window.png) that shows our scheduled window; it may overlap the customer-observed window. We'll coordinate a joint post-mortem and get back with an attribution percentage for credit calculation.

Regards,
Sean Gallagher
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.ai

Date: 2026-11-01T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: Midwest Payments credit — attribution proposal

Team,

Summary: Midwest Payments has requested an SLA credit for the 2026-10-28 partial degradation. External provider NetworkX reports a BGP flap 01:10–01:38 UTC; we had a planned routing resync 01:00–01:45 UTC. Client-observed window per Alex: ~01:12–01:57 UTC. Correlated traces show error spike 01:12–01:50 UTC with heavier error concentrations at 01:15–01:35 UTC.

Preliminary attribution:
- NetworkX (third-party): ~60% of impact (packet loss/path instability in their POPs).
- Redwood routing resync (our maintenance): ~40% contributing to latency amplification and retries.

SLA math: Client's affected duration we consider within SLA calculation = 38 minutes attributable to our service (net of third-party exclusion) => per contract that would be partial credit of 50% of the formulaic amount.

Options:
A) Offer formulaic credit (50% of calculated credit) — defendable by logs and exclusions.
B) Offer full credit as a one-time goodwill concession to preserve the account (Midwest is mid-enterprise, expanding usage next quarter).

Requesting approval: Marissa (sales) — recommend full credit to keep renewal momentum. Kimberly (legal/finance) — confirm billing mechanics and any precedent concerns. Karthik (SRE) — confirm the 60/40 split is reasonable from infra logs.

Attaching: networkx_bgp_dump.txt, mp_errors_oct28.log, slo_routing_maintenance_window.png for reference.

Thanks,
Sean

Subject: Re: Transaction API errors + high latency 2026-10-28 (SLA credit decision)

Hi Alex —

Thanks for the patience while we completed the investigation. We appreciate the logs you shared — that made correlation much faster. Summary of findings:
- NetworkX reported a BGP flap that affected a subset of paths between 01:10–01:38 UTC.
- Redwood performed a scheduled routing resync 01:00–01:45 UTC which, when combined with the external instability, lengthened the effective degradation window.

Attribution and credit: per the SLA and the investigation, we attribute approximately 60% of the impact to NetworkX and 40% to Redwood. Under the contract's third-party exclusion language this would normally reduce the SLA credit proportionally.

Resolution: Redwood will issue a credit equal to 50% of the contractual SLA credit amount for the impacted billing period as a gesture of goodwill to support your operational continuity while you evaluate route asymmetry mitigations with NetworkX. The credit will be applied to your next invoice; schedule attached (credit_schedule.pdf).

Next steps we recommend jointly:
- We will coordinate a tri-party post-mortem with NetworkX to reduce recurrence risk.
- If you prefer, we can schedule a short architecture review to discuss peering and retry/backoff tuning to minimize future user impact.

Please confirm receipt and let us know whether the proposed credit and post-mortem plan are acceptable.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Head of Enterprise Accounts, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
